questiontext.text: Which set contains the three infrastructure pillars introduced in the lecture?

generalfeedback.text: Compute executes workloads, storage retains data, and networking connects resources. The alternatives describe activities, environments, or application-level concerns rather than the three infrastructure pillars.

answer.text: Deployment, testing, and monitoring
Compute, storage, and network
Development, testing, and production
Applications, users, and source code

questiontext.text: Which statement best describes a declarative infrastructure definition?

generalfeedback.text: A declarative definition expresses the intended state. Automation determines the operations needed from the declaration and actual state. Declarative syntax alone does not remove dependencies or guarantee parallel execution.

answer.text: It records every command an administrator previously executed.
It specifies the exact sequence of operations for every starting state.
It describes the desired state, while automation determines how to reach it.
It guarantees that every operation can run in parallel.

questiontext.text: An automation run has successfully reached the desired state. Its inputs and the relevant external state then remain unchanged. What should a second idempotent run do?

generalfeedback.text: Once the desired state is satisfied, repeating an idempotent operation under unchanged relevant conditions should cause no further managed-state changes. Checking the current state is compatible with idempotence; doing nothing without checking does not establish correctness.

answer.text: Leave the managed state unchanged because it already satisfies the declaration.
Recreate all resources to prove they can be recreated.
Skip checking the current state and report success.
Add another copy of each declared resource.

questiontext.text: A team moves from managing virtual machines under IaaS to a managed application platform under PaaS. Which responsibility would typically move towards the provider?

generalfeedback.text: PaaS typically transfers more operating-system and runtime-platform maintenance to the provider. The exact boundary depends on the service. The application team still owns its business requirements and application code.

answer.text: Deciding the application's business requirements
Maintaining the team's application source code
Choosing which application features to release
Maintaining more of the underlying operating system and runtime platform

questiontext.text: Which pair of benefits best explains how version-controlling infrastructure definitions helps a team deliver changes reliably?

generalfeedback.text: Review before application can catch mistakes, and a traceable history helps explain and investigate changes. Version control alone neither applies changes nor restores deleted data; reviewed changes still need validation.

answer.text: It preserves change history and makes reverting a definition sufficient to restore deleted application data.
It provides a shared definition and keeps running infrastructure synchronized whenever a change is committed.
It makes proposed changes reviewable and records who changed the intended configuration and why.
It makes environment differences visible and makes validation unnecessary after a change is approved.

questiontext.text: Two servers were created from the same definition. An administrator changes a managed setting manually on one server. Which description and response best address the situation?

generalfeedback.text: Drift is a difference between actual managed state and intended state. Investigate it before reconciliation: an unauthorized change may need reversal, while a legitimate change should be reviewed and recorded in the definition. A shared origin does not guarantee continued consistency.

answer.text: The server has drifted from the declared state; compare the difference and either restore the approved setting or review and update the definition.
The definition has become obsolete; copy the changed setting into it and apply it to the other server without further review.
The servers are still consistent because they share an original definition; record the manual change only in an operational log.
The difference is necessarily a fault; rebuild both servers immediately without checking why the setting was changed.

name.text: L1 Q7 Mutable and immutable infrastructure

questiontext.text: A server needs an operating-system configuration change and stores application data that must survive the update. Which plan correctly distinguishes mutable and immutable approaches?

generalfeedback.text: Mutable updates change an existing instance. Immutable updates replace it with an instance prepared from the updated definition or image. Persistent application data needs separate storage or a verified transfer/recovery process; infrastructure definitions do not generally contain that data.

answer.text: A mutable update replaces the server; an immutable update modifies the existing server while preserving its identity.
Both approaches modify the existing server; the immutable approach additionally records the change in version control.
A mutable update changes the existing server; an immutable update replaces it and recreates persistent data from the infrastructure definition.
A mutable update changes the existing server; an immutable update replaces it and preserves persistent data separately or through a verified migration.

name.text: L1 Q8 Separating infrastructure and server configuration

questiontext.text: A deployment needs networks and virtual machines, plus software and service configuration inside those machines. Which organization best separates responsibilities while keeping the deployment coordinated?

generalfeedback.text: Provisioning establishes resources and connectivity; server configuration establishes software, files, and service state. Clear boundaries with explicit information flow support focused review and reuse. Separate repositories are optional and do not by themselves keep dependencies synchronized.

answer.text: Maintain each environment as a complete independent copy so changes to shared configuration never affect another environment.
Separate resource provisioning from server configuration, pass required resource information between them, and review each concern independently.
Put provisioning and configuration in separate repositories and rely on operators to keep their connection details synchronized.
Keep only resource provisioning in code and document the manual software setup as the interface between the two responsibilities.

name.text: L1 Q9 Dependencies and changing resource information

questiontext.text: An application server requires a network. A later configuration step needs the server's assigned address, which may change when the server is replaced. The team currently copies that address into several files. Which design best preserves both dependency order and current connection information?

generalfeedback.text: Explicit dependencies identify what must exist or be known before another step can proceed. Passing current resource outputs avoids stale, duplicated addresses after replacement. File names alone do not encode those resource relationships, and correct ordering alone does not keep copied values current.

answer.text: Represent network-to-server and server-to-configuration dependencies explicitly, and derive the connection address from the current server output.
Number the definition files in deployment order, and retain the original address as a default in each configuration file.
Start all stages together, and retry configuration against the previously recorded address until the server becomes reachable.
Create the network and server in order, and let each configuration stage maintain its own reviewed copy of the assigned address.

name.text: L1 Q10 Shared definitions and environment differences

questiontext.text: Development and production use copied infrastructure definitions. They should share an application structure, but production needs greater capacity. Independent edits have introduced differences whose purpose is unclear. Which approach best preserves legitimate differences and prevents accidental divergence?

generalfeedback.text: A shared definition captures the common structure, while explicit environment values retain intended capacity differences. Compare definitions and actual state with the agreed design, then review and validate changes. Identical values are not required, and undocumented manual exceptions undermine the shared source of truth.

answer.text: Keep independent definitions and periodically copy production over development, treating production capacity as the shared baseline.
Require identical definitions and values everywhere, recording production capacity changes only in an operational checklist.
Share the common structure, keep environment values explicit, and review existing differences against intended state before validating future changes.
Create a shared definition, permit manual environment-specific changes after deployment, and review only changes to the shared definition.
